레이스.etymology: Borrowed from English lace ('delicate openwork fabric', via Old French las from Latin laqueus 'noose, snare'); also homophonous with English race.

렌즈.etymology: Borrowed from English lens (from Latin lēns, 'lentil', because a double-convex glass lens resembles the shape of a lentil seed).

history.meaning: lens (optical lens, camera lens, contact lens)

렌치.etymology: Borrowed from English wrench, a hand tool used to grip and turn nuts or bolts.

history.meaning: tool for turning nuts and bolts

렌틸콩.etymology: Hybrid compound combining English loanword 렌틸 (lentil, from Old French lentille < Latin lēns) with native Korean 콩 ('bean, legume').
렌틸콩.notes: Shares its ultimate Latin root lēns ('lentil') with 렌즈 (lens), named for its biconvex lentil shape.

로비.etymology: Borrowed from English lobby, referring to the entrance hall or foyer of a hotel, theater, or large building.

롤.etymology: Borrowed from English roll, referring to a cylindrical roll of paper, fabric, or bread.

history.meaning: something rolled into a cylinder; bread roll

를.etymology: Native Korean accusative (direct object) case particle used after vowel-final nouns, descending from Middle Korean 랄 / 를 (allomorph of 을).

리듬.etymology: Borrowed from English rhythm (ultimately from Ancient Greek rhythmós, 'measured motion, symmetry').

리본.etymology: Borrowed from English ribbon, referring to a narrow strip of fabric tied in a bow or used as trim.

링.etymology: Borrowed from English ring, denoting a circular metal band, hoop, or key ring.

마다하다.etymology: Native Korean verb lexicalized from 말다 ('to desist, decline') + declarative/quotative -다 + 하다 (literally 'to say no to, decline to do').

history.meaning: to refuse, turn down, shrink from (often in 마다하지 않다 'not hesitate/refuse')

마디.etymology: Native Korean noun descending from Middle Korean 마대 ('joint or node of bamboo/bone; knot; musical measure; phrase of speech').

history.meaning: joint, node; musical bar/measure; word/phrase (한 마디)

마룻바닥.etymology: Native Korean compound noun combining 마루 (Middle Korean 마루, 'raised wooden floor') + compound linker -ㅅ- (saisiot) + 바닥 ('floor, bottom surface').

마르다.etymology: Native Korean ㄹ-irregular verb descending from Middle Korean 마르다 ('to become dry, dry up, grow thin').

history.meaning: to dry, run dry, become thin

마법.etymology: Sino-Korean 마법 (魔法), compounding 마 (魔, 'demon, supernatural spirit') and 법 (法, 'art, method, law').

마시다.etymology: Native Korean verb descending from Middle Korean 마시다 ('to drink liquid, breathe in').

마음.etymology: Native Korean noun descending from Middle Korean 마음 ('heart, mind, inner spirit, intention').

마주.etymology: Native Korean adverb descending from Middle Korean 마조, derived from the stem 맞- of 맞다 ('to face, meet') + adverbial suffix -오/-우.

history.meaning: face to face, opposite each other

마지막.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'the last, final moment or item', formed from the stem of 마치다/맞다 ('to finish, conclude') + nominal suffix -막.

마침.etymology: Native Korean adverb descending from Middle Korean 마참 / 마침, related to 맞다 ('to fit the moment, hit the mark') and 마치다 ('to finish').

history.meaning: just then, opportunely, as it happened

마트.etymology: Borrowed from English mart (popularized in South Korea via discount-store chains and clipped from supermarket).

막다.etymology: Native Korean verb descending from Middle Korean 막다 ('to block, stop up, obstruct, keep out').

history.meaning: to block, stop, prevent, shield from

막히다.etymology: Native Korean passive verb descending from Middle Korean 막히다, formed from 막다 ('to block') + passive suffix -히-.

history.meaning: to be blocked, clogged, congested, deadlocked

만.etymology: Sino-Korean numeral 만 (萬, 'ten thousand, 10,000'), from Middle Chinese *mjonH; also homophonous with the native restrictive particle/bound noun 만 ('only, just; elapsed time since').

history.meaning: ten thousand (10,000); only/just; after an interval of

만나다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb descending from Middle Korean 맛나다, formed from 맞- ('to face, meet') + 나다 ('to come forth, occur'), with nasal assimilation of ㅅ + ㄴ > ㄴ + ㄴ.

만남.etymology: Native Korean deverbal noun formed from 만나다 ('to meet') + nominalizing suffix -ㅁ.

만들다.etymology: Native Korean ㄹ-stem verb descending from Middle Korean 맹글다 / 만들다 ('to make, craft, build, form').

만실.etymology: Sino-Korean 만실 (滿室), compounding 만 (滿, 'full') and 실 (室, 'room, guestroom').

만약.etymology: Sino-Korean 만약 (萬若), compounding 만 (萬, 'ten thousand [possibilities]') and 약 (若, 'if, suppose').

history.meaning: if by one chance in ten thousand
if, in case, by any chance

만점.etymology: Sino-Korean 만점 (滿點), compounding 만 (滿, 'full, complete') and 점 (點, 'point, score, mark').

history.meaning: full marks, perfect score, ten out of ten

만지다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to touch, feel, or handle with the hand', attested in Early Modern Korean as 만지다 alongside Middle Korean 만히다 ('to stroke, rub, touch').

history.meaning: to stroke, rub, touch with the hand

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 만지다

만하다.etymology: Native Korean auxiliary adjective ('worth doing, big enough to') formed from the bound noun 만 ('extent, degree, comparable size', Middle Korean 만) plus the adjective-forming verb 하다.

history.meaning: to be of such an extent or worth
to be worth doing; to be the size of

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 만하다

많다.etymology: Native Korean adjective descending from Middle Korean 만ᄒᆞ다 ('to be many, abundant'), contracted by syncope of the vowel ᆞ between ㄴ and ㅎ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 많다

많이.etymology: Native Korean adverb derived from the adjective stem 많- ('many, much') plus the productive adverbial suffix -이 (Middle Korean 만히).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 많이

morphemes.meaning: in such a manner or degree

말.etymology: Core native Korean noun with three major homophonous lineages: (1) 'speech, word, language' (Middle Korean 말, low-rising tone); (2) 'horse' (Middle Korean ᄆᆞᆯ); and (3) a traditional dry volume measure equal to ten 되 (~18 liters, Middle Korean 말).

history.meaning: word, speech, language; horse; unit of measure

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 말

말다.etymology: Native Korean ㄹ-stem verb representing two distinct Middle Korean roots: (1) auxiliary and main verb 'to stop, cease, refrain from' (used in prohibitions with -지 말다, Middle Korean 말다); and (2) 'to roll up, wrap' or 'to mix rice or noodles into broth' (Middle Korean 몰다 / 말다).

history.meaning: to cease, refrain from; to roll up
to stop, refrain from (-지 말다); to roll up; to steep in broth

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 말다

말씀.etymology: Native Korean noun derived from 말 ('speech, words') with the historical nominalizing suffix -ᄊᆞᆷ / -씀, attested in 15th-century Hunminjeongeum texts as 말ᄊᆞᆷ.
말씀.notes: In modern Korean, 말씀 both elevates an elder's or guest's words (선생님 말씀) and humbles one's own (제가 말씀드릴게요).

말씀드리다.etymology: Humble compound verb meaning 'to speak or tell (to a respected person)', combining native Korean 말씀 ('words, speech', from Middle Korean 말ᄊᆞᆷ) with the humble benefactive verb 드리다 ('to give/offer to a superior').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 말씀드리다

morphemes.meaning: to give or offer to a superior

말씀하다.etymology: Verb formed from native Korean 말씀 ('words, speech', from Middle Korean 말ᄊᆞᆷ, originally a general nominalization of 말 'speech' + -ᄊᆞᆷ that later specialized for honorific and humble registers) plus verbalizer -하다.

history.meaning: to speak, say (honorific as 말씀하시다 or humble)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 말씀하다

말하다.etymology: Transparent native Korean verb combining 말 ('word, speech, language', Middle Korean 말) with the verbalizer -하다 ('to do, make').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 말하다

맑다.etymology: Native Korean adjective descending from Middle Korean ᄆᆞᇰ다 ('clear, limpid, pure, sunny'), with regular shift of ᆞ to ㅏ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맑다

맛.etymology: Native Korean noun descending directly from Middle Korean 맛 ('taste, flavor, relish').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맛

맛보다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb joining 맛 ('taste, flavor') and 보다 ('to see, try, experience'), attested since Middle Korean 맛보다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맛보다

맛있다.etymology: Native Korean compound adjective literally meaning 'taste exists' or 'having flavor', formed from 맛 ('taste, flavor') + 있다 ('to exist, have').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맛있다

맞다.etymology: Native Korean verb from Middle Korean 맞다 ('to meet, face; to match, be correct; to be struck by'), underlying a family of causative derivatives (맞추다, 맞히다) and compounds (맞이하다).

history.meaning: to meet, match, be right, be hit
to be correct/right; to fit; to greet; to be hit

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맞다

맞이하다.etymology: Native Korean verb formed from 맞이 ('act of welcoming or receiving', derived from 맞다 'to meet, greet' + nominalizing suffix -이) plus verbalizer -하다.

history.meaning: to go out to meet, welcome

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맞이하다

맞추다.etymology: Native Korean causative verb derived from 맞- ('to fit, match, meet') plus the causative/transitive suffix -추- (Middle Korean 마초다), meaning 'to bring into alignment, adjust, assemble, or custom-order'.

history.meaning: to fit, adjust, set, assemble, order custom-made

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맞추다

맞히다.etymology: Native Korean causative verb derived from 맞- ('to be correct; to be struck') plus the causative suffix -히- (Middle Korean 마키다 / 맛치다), meaning 'to hit a target, guess an answer correctly, or expose to rain/snow'.

history.meaning: to hit a mark, cause to be struck
to guess right, hit the mark

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맞히다

맡기다.etymology: Native Korean causative verb derived from 맡- ('to take charge of, undertake') plus the causative suffix -기- (Middle Korean 맛기다), meaning 'to entrust, leave in another's care, deposit'.

history.meaning: to entrust, commit to someone's care
to entrust, leave with, check in

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맡기다

맡다.etymology: Native Korean verb uniting two Middle Korean verbs that merged in Modern Korean orthography: (1) 맛다 ('to take charge of, undertake responsibility for') and (2) 맡다 ('to smell, sniff, perceive an odor').

history.meaning: to take charge of; to smell, sniff
to take charge of, handle; to smell, sniff

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맡다

매끄럽다.etymology: Native Korean ㅂ-irregular adjective meaning 'smooth, sleek, slippery', formed from an expressive root 매끌-/미끌- (compare 미끄럽다 'slippery' and 매끈하다 'sleek') plus the adjective-forming suffix -업다/-럽다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매끄럽다

매년.etymology: Sino-Korean time noun and adverb 매년 (每年), meaning 'every year, annually', composed of 每 (매, 'each, every') + 年 (년, 'year').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매년

매니저.etymology: Borrowed from English manager ('person who manages a business, store, team, or performer').

history.meaning: person responsible for controlling or administering an organization

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매니저

매다.etymology: Native Korean verb descending from Middle Korean ᄆᆡ다 ('to tie, bind, fasten; to weed'), with regular monophthongization of ㆎ (ᆞㅣ) to ㅐ.

history.meaning: to tie, fasten, tighten (a shoelace, belt, or strap)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매다

매달리다.etymology: Native Korean passive/intransitive verb derived from 매달다 ('to tie and hang up', a compound of 매다 'to tie' + 달다 'to suspend') plus the passive suffix -리-.

history.meaning: to hang from, cling to, be absorbed in

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매달리다

매물.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 매물 (賣物), literally 'an article or property put up for sale', formed from 賣 (매, 'to sell') + 物 (물, 'thing, object, property').

history.meaning: goods or property offered for sale
item for sale, real estate listing

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매물

매수자.etymology: Sino-Korean legal and commercial term 매수자 (買受者), meaning 'buyer, purchaser', formed from 매수 (買受, 'buying and taking delivery') + agent suffix -자 (者, 'person').

history.meaning: person who buys and receives property

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매수자

매일.etymology: Sino-Korean noun and adverb 매일 (每日), meaning 'every day, daily', from 每 (매, 'each, every') + 日 (일, 'day').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매일

매주.etymology: Sino-Korean noun and adverb 매주 (每週), meaning 'every week, weekly', from 每 (매, 'each, every') + 週 (주, 'week, cycle').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 매주

맨.etymology: Native Korean determiner from Middle Korean ᄆᆡᆫ, used in two related senses: (1) before nouns of position or order to mean 'the very, the extreme/topmost' (e.g., 맨 위 'the very top', 맨 처음 'the very beginning'); and (2) as a prefixal determiner meaning 'bare, unmixed' (e.g., 맨손 'bare hands').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 맨

머그잔.etymology: Hybrid compound noun combining English loanword 머그 (mug) with Sino-Korean 잔 (盞, 'cup, goblet') to specify a handled cylindrical mug.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 머그잔

머리.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'head; hair on the head; mind; top/beginning', descending from Middle Korean 마리 ('head') through vowel assimilation (마리 > 머리).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 머리

머물다.etymology: Native Korean verb (contracted variant of 머무르다) meaning 'to stay, remain, lodge, linger', descending from Middle Korean 머믈다 ('to halt, stay, tarry').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 머물다

머신.etymology: Direct loanword from English machine, commonly used in compounds such as 커피 머신 ('coffee/espresso machine') or 러닝머신 ('treadmill').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 머신

먹다.etymology: Core native Korean verb meaning 'to eat, consume, take in', attested unchanged in form since Middle Korean 먹다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 먹다

먼저.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'first, ahead, beforehand', descending from Middle Korean 몬져 ('first, before others').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 먼저

먼지.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'dust, fine dirt particles', attested in Early Modern Korean as 먼지 (replacing earlier Middle Korean 믜리 / 드틀).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 먼지

멀리.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'far, far away, in the distance', derived from the adjective stem 멀- (멀다, 'to be far') plus the adverbial suffix -리, attested in Middle Korean as 멀리.

history.meaning: far, afar, a long way off

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 멀리

멀쩡하다.etymology: Native Korean adjective meaning 'completely intact, unharmed, perfectly fine, or shamelessly composed', formed from the expressive root 멀쩡- (dark-vowel counterpart of 말짱-) plus -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 멀쩡하다

멈추다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to stop, halt, cease', historically derived from the intransitive root 멎- ('to cease, stop') with a causative/intensive suffix (Middle Korean 머추다, later nasalized to 멈추다).

history.meaning: to stop, halt, cause to cease

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 멈추다

멋지다.etymology: Native Korean compound adjective meaning 'stylish, wonderful, splendid, cool', formed from 멋 ('style, charm, refined taste, flair') + -지다 ('to be endowed with, full of').

history.meaning: full of charm or refined taste

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 멋지다

멎다.etymology: Native Korean intransitive verb meaning 'to stop, cease, abate' (especially of rain, snow, wind, bleeding, or sound), descending directly from Middle Korean 멎다.

history.meaning: to stop, cease, come to a halt

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 멎다

메뉴.etymology: Borrowed from English and French menu ('bill of fare in a restaurant; list of options'), ultimately from Latin minutus ('small, detailed list').

history.meaning: detailed list of dishes served at a meal

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 메뉴

메뉴판.etymology: Hybrid compound noun combining the loanword 메뉴 (menu) with Sino-Korean 판 (板, 'board, plaque, sheet'), denoting a physical menu board or printed menu card.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 메뉴판

메모.etymology: Borrowed from English memo (clipping of memorandum, 'something to be remembered; brief written note').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 메모

메시지.etymology: Borrowed from English message ('verbal, written, or electronic communication; underlying theme'), ultimately from Old French message.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 메시지

메아리.etymology: Native Korean, from Middle Korean 뫼ᅀᅡ리 (mwǒyzàlí), which Wiktionary analyses as 'one who lives in the mountains' (뫼 'mountain' + 살- 'live' + agentive -이).
메아리.notes: The echo was pictured as a voice answering from the mountains.

멜로디.etymology: Borrowed from English melody ('sequence of musical notes forming a tune'), ultimately from Ancient Greek μελῳδία (melōidía, 'choral song').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 멜로디

명.etymology: Sino-Korean bound noun and classifier 명 (名) used to count people ('person, people'), originally meaning 'name, roll entry'; also used as an independent Sino-Korean noun meaning 'name, renown' (名) or 'life, fate, command' (命).

history.meaning: name; person on a roster -> classifier for people

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 명

명판.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 명판 (銘板 / 名板), meaning 'nameplate, identification plate, inscribed plaque', formed from 銘 (명, 'inscribe, engraving') or 名 (명, 'name') + 板 (판, 'plate, board').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 명판

몇.etymology: Native Korean interrogative and indefinite determiner meaning 'how many; a few, several', descending from Middle Korean 몃.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 몇

몇십.etymology: Hybrid compound numeral combining native Korean 몇 ('how many; several') with Sino-Korean 십 (十, 'ten'), meaning 'several tens, dozens, or how many tens'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 몇십

모금.etymology: Native Korean classifier noun meaning 'a mouthful, sip (of liquid), or puff (of smoke)', derived by vowel shift from Middle Korean 머굼, the nominalized form (-움) of 머금다 ('to hold in the mouth'). Also homophonous with Sino-Korean 모금 (募金, 'fundraising').

history.meaning: mouthful (from 머금다 'to hold in the mouth')

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모금

모닝빵.etymology: South Korean hybrid compound combining English loanword 모닝 (morning) with 빵 ('bread', borrowed via Japanese パン from Portuguese pão), denoting a small, soft, slightly sweet dinner/breakfast roll.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모닝빵

모닝커피.etymology: Compound loanword from English morning coffee ('a cup of coffee drunk in the morning to start the day').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모닝커피

모두.etymology: Native Korean adverb and noun meaning 'all, everyone, everything', descending from Middle Korean 모도 ('all together'), an adverbial derivation from the verb root 믇- / 모도- ('to gather, assemble').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모두

모든.etymology: Native Korean determiner meaning 'all, every', fossilized from the adnominal form (모ᄃᆞᆫ) of the Middle Korean intransitive verb 몯다 ('to come together, gather, assemble').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모든

모르다.etymology: Native Korean 르-irregular verb meaning 'not to know, be unaware of, be unable to tell', descending from Middle Korean 모ᄅᆞ다.

history.meaning: not to know, be ignorant of
not to know, be unaware of

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모르다

모서리.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'corner, sharp edge (of a table, box, or stone)', formed from 모 ('angle, corner', Middle Korean 모ㅎ) + 서리 ('edge, border, area around').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모서리

모서리용.etymology: Hybrid compound noun combining native Korean 모서리 ('corner, edge') with the Sino-Korean suffix -용 (用, 'for the use of'), meaning 'for corners, corner-use (e.g., corner guards or corner shelves)'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모서리용

모으다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb meaning 'to gather, collect, save up, assemble', descending from Middle Korean 모호다 ('to bring together', causative counterpart of 믇다 'to gather').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모으다

모이다.etymology: Native Korean intransitive/passive verb meaning 'to gather, assemble, come together', descending from Middle Korean 모히다 (derived from 모호다 'to gather' + passive suffix -이-).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모이다

모퉁이.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'corner, bend, turn (of a street, wall, or building)', derived from 모 ('angle, corner', Middle Korean 모ㅎ, which carries final ㅎ accounting for the aspirated ㅌ) plus the locative/expressive suffix -웅이.

history.meaning: street corner, bend, angle of a wall

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 모퉁이

목공풀.etymology: Hybrid compound of Sino-Korean 목공 (木工, 'woodworking, carpentry') and native 풀 ('glue, paste').
목공풀.notes: Pronounced [목꽁풀] with compound tensification of 목 + 공.

목록.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 목록 (目錄), meaning 'list, catalog, inventory, table of contents', from 目 (목, 'eye; item, heading') + 錄 (록, 'record, register, copy').

history.meaning: written register of items or headings

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 목록

목소리.etymology: Native Korean compound of 목 ('throat, neck') and 소리 ('sound').
목소리.notes: Distinguishes a human speaking or singing voice from general 소리 ('sound, noise').

목수.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 목수 (木手), meaning 'carpenter, woodworker', attested since Joseon-era records, from 木 (목, 'wood, timber') + 手 (수, 'hand; skilled craftsperson').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 목수

목요일.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 목요일 (木曜日), built from 목 (木, 'tree, wood / Jupiter'), 요 (曜, 'luminary'), and 일 (日, 'day').
목요일.notes: Pronounced [모교일] via smooth liaison of final ㄱ onto initial ㅇ.

목조.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 목조 (木造), meaning 'wooden construction, built of wood', formed from 木 (목, 'wood, timber') + 造 (조, 'make, build, construct').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 목조

몫.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'share, allotted portion, role, quota', descending from Middle Korean 몫 / 몯 ('share, division, lot').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 몫

몰래.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'secretly, stealthily, on the sly', historically fossilized from the stem 모르- (모르다, 'not to know') + adverbial suffix -애 (Middle Korean 몰래, literally 'without others knowing').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 몰래

몸.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'body; physical health; main part', attested unchanged in form since Middle Korean 몸.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 몸

못.etymology: Native Korean negative adverb meaning 'cannot, unable to' (descending from Middle Korean 몯). Homophonous with native Korean nouns 못 ('nail, spike, peg', Middle Korean 못) and 못 ('pond, pool', Middle Korean 못).

history.meaning: cannot, unable to (몯); nail, peg; pond (못)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 못

못하다.etymology: Native Korean verb and auxiliary verb meaning 'to be unable to do; to fall short of, be inferior to; to do poorly', formed by fusing the negative adverb 못 (Middle Korean 몯, 'cannot') with 하다 ('to do, be').

history.meaning: to be unable to do; to be inferior
cannot do; to be worse at / inferior to

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 못하다

묘하다.etymology: Sino-Korean adjective formed from 묘 (妙, 'subtle, mysterious, exquisite, peculiar') plus the adjective-forming verb -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 묘하다

무겁다.etymology: Native Korean ㅂ-irregular adjective meaning 'heavy, weighty, grave', descending directly from Middle Korean 무겁다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무겁다

무뚝뚝하다.etymology: Native Korean adjective meaning 'blunt, brusque, curt, uncommunicative', formed from an expressive stem 무뚝뚝- (intensifying prefix 무- + reduplicated ideophone 뚝뚝 'abrupt, gruff') plus -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무뚝뚝하다

무료.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 무료 (無料), meaning 'free of charge, complimentary, no fee', composed of 無 (무, 'without, none') + 料 (료, 'fee, charge, fare').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무료

무사하다.etymology: Sino-Korean adjective formed from 무사 (無事, literally 'without incident or trouble') plus -하다, meaning 'safe, unharmed, peaceful'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무사하다

무섭다.etymology: Native Korean ㅂ-irregular adjective meaning 'scary, frightening; fearful, afraid', descending from Middle Korean 무셥다 ('fearsome, dreadful').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무섭다

무슨.etymology: Native Korean interrogative and indefinite determiner meaning 'what, what kind of, some', descending from Middle Korean 무슨 / 므슴 (adnominal derivative of the interrogative root 므스- 'what').

history.meaning: what, what kind of; some, any

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무슨

무엇.etymology: Native Korean interrogative and indefinite pronoun meaning 'what, something', contracted from Middle Korean 므스것 (므스 'what' + 것 'thing' -> 므엇 -> 무엇).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무엇

무염.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 무염 (無鹽), meaning 'unsalted, salt-free' (frequently used of culinary ingredients such as 무염 버터 'unsalted butter'), formed from 無 (무, 'without') + 鹽 (염, 'salt').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 무염

묵다.etymology: Native Korean verb descending from Middle Korean 묵다 ('to stay overnight, lodge; to remain long, age, become old or fermented').

history.meaning: to stay over, remain long, age
to stay overnight, lodge; to age, ferment

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 묵다

묶이다.etymology: Native Korean passive verb meaning 'to be tied, bound, bundled, or restricted', derived from 묶다 ('to tie, bind, bundle', Middle Korean 믜다 / 묶다) plus the passive suffix -이-.

history.meaning: to be tied, bound, bundled, held up

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 묶이다

문.etymology: Sino-Korean noun 문 (門, Middle Chinese *mwon*), meaning 'door, gate, entrance, opening', borrowed early and serving as the standard everyday Korean word for 'door'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 문

문장.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 문장 (文章), meaning 'sentence (in grammar); prose composition, writing style', from 文 (문, 'writing, characters') + 章 (장, 'section, composition, emblem').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 문장

문제.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 문제 (問題), meaning 'question (on a test); problem, issue, matter for discussion', from 問 (문, 'to ask, inquire') + 題 (제, 'topic, subject, heading').

history.meaning: question posed for answer or debate

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 문제

문턱.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'threshold, doorsill', combining Sino-Korean 문 (門, 'door, gate') with native Korean 턱 ('raised ridge, sill, chin').

history.meaning: threshold, doorsill; figurative barrier to entry

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 문턱

문화유산과.etymology: Sino-Korean administrative compound 문화유산과 (文化遺産課), meaning 'Cultural Heritage Division/Section', formed from 문화 (文化, 'culture') + 유산 (遺産, 'heritage, legacy') + -과 (課, 'administrative department or section').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 문화유산과

묻다.etymology: Native Korean verb representing three Middle Korean verbs that share the modern citation spelling 묻다: (1) ㄷ-irregular 묻다 ('to ask, inquire', stem 물어- before vowels, Middle Korean 묻다); (2) regular 묻다 ('to bury in the ground, conceal', Middle Korean 묻다); and (3) regular 묻다 ('to stick to, stain, get smeared on', Middle Korean 묻다).

history.meaning: to ask (ㄷ-stem); to bury; to adhere/stain
to ask, inquire; to bury; to get on, stain

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 묻다

물.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'water, liquid, stream', descending from Middle Korean 믈 ('water') via Early Modern Korean labial rounding of ㅡ to ㅜ after the bilabial nasal ㅁ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물

물건.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 물건 (物件), meaning 'thing, object, item, goods', formed from 物 (물, 'thing, object, matter') + 件 (건, 'article, item').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물건

물러가다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to step back, retreat, withdraw, leave a superior's presence', combining the infinitive stem 물러- of 무르다 ('to move back, yield') with 가다 ('to go').

history.meaning: to step back, fall back, retire

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물러가다

물러서다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to step back, stand back, back down, resign from a post', combining 물러- (from 무르다, 'to move back') with 서다 ('to stand', Middle Korean 셔다).

history.meaning: to step back, back away, step down

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물러서다

물론.etymology: Sino-Korean noun and adverb 물론 (勿論), meaning 'of course, needless to say, not to mention', literally 'do not discuss or argue', from 勿 (물, 'do not') + 論 (론, 'discuss, debate').

history.meaning: no need to debate -> without question
of course, naturally, needless to say

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물론

물어보다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to ask, inquire', formed from the ㄷ-irregular verb 묻다 ('to ask', conjugated as 물어-) plus the exploratory auxiliary verb 보다 ('to try, see').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물어보다

물체.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 물체 (物體), meaning 'physical object, body, material form', composed of 物 (물, 'thing, matter') + 體 (체, 'body, substance, form').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 물체

뭐.etymology: Colloquial native Korean pronoun and interjection meaning 'what; something; well', contracted from 무엇 ('what', Middle Korean 므스것 > 므엇 > 무엇 > 무어 > 뭐).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뭐

미끄러지다.etymology: Native Korean intransitive verb meaning 'to slip, slide, skid', derived from the adjective 미끄럽다 ('slippery', Middle Korean 밋그럽다) plus the inchoative auxiliary verb -어지다.

history.meaning: to slip, slide on a smooth surface

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 미끄러지다

미나.etymology: Korean female given name 미나, typically written in Sino-Korean characters such as 美娜 ('beautiful and graceful') or 美奈.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 미나

미리.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'in advance, beforehand, ahead of time', attested unchanged since Middle Korean 미리.

history.meaning: in advance, beforehand, ahead of time

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 미리

미완성.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 미완성 (未完成), attaching negative prefix 미- (未, 'not yet') to 완성 (完成, 'completion').

미터.etymology: Borrowed from English meter / metre ('the fundamental SI unit of length'), ultimately from French mètre and Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron, 'measure').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 미터

민수.etymology: Common Korean given name 민수, typically written with Sino-Korean hanja combinations such as 民秀 ('outstanding among the people') or 敏秀 ('clever and outstanding').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 민수

민트차.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'mint tea', combining the English loanword 민트 (mint) with Sino-Korean 차 (茶, 'tea').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 민트차

믿다.etymology: Native Korean regular verb meaning 'to believe, trust, have faith in', descending unchanged in form from Middle Korean 믿다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 믿다

밀다.etymology: Native Korean ㄹ-stem verb meaning 'to push, shove, slide, plane/roll out', descending directly from Middle Korean 밀다.

history.meaning: to push, slide, roll out (dough), shave

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밀다

밀리미터.etymology: Borrowed from English millimeter / millimetre ('one thousandth of a meter', from Latin mille 'thousand' + meter).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밀리미터

밑.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'bottom, underside, base, foot (of a mountain or object)', descending directly from Middle Korean 밑 ('base, bottom, root').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밑

바구니.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'woven basket', descending from Middle Korean 바고니 via vowel raising (바고니 > 바구니).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바구니

바깥.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'the outside, exterior, outdoors', historically formed as a reduplicated or intensive derivative of 밖 ('outside', Middle Korean 밧ㄱ-).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바깥

바깥쪽.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'the outside, outer side, exterior direction', formed from 바깥 ('outside, exterior') + 쪽 ('side, direction').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바깥쪽

바꾸다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb meaning 'to change, exchange, swap, replace', descending from Middle Korean 바꾸다 / 바꼬다 ('to barter, exchange, alter').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바꾸다

바뀌다.etymology: Native Korean passive/intransitive verb meaning 'to change, be changed, shift, be replaced', derived from 바꾸다 ('to change, exchange') plus the passive suffix -이-.

history.meaning: to change, be altered, turn into

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바뀌다

바다.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'sea, ocean', descending from Middle Korean 바닿 (and archaic variant 바ᄅᆞᆯ).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바다

바닥.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'floor, bottom surface, ground, sole (of the foot or shoe), palm (of the hand)', attested since Early Modern Korean 바닥.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바닥

바라다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to wish, hope for, desire; to look toward', descending from Middle Korean 바라다 ('to hope for, gaze toward').

history.meaning: to look toward, hope for, desire

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바라다

바람.etymology: Native Korean noun with two distinct etymologies: (1) 'wind, breeze' (descending from Middle Korean 바ᄅᆞᆷ via loss of ᆞ); and (2) 'wish, hope, expectation' (substantive derivation of 바라다 'to wish, hope' + nominalizer -ㅁ).

history.meaning: wind, air current; that which is hoped for

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바람

바로.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'straight, directly, right away, precisely, none other than', descending from Middle Korean 바ᄅᆞ, the adverbial derivative of 바ᄅᆞ다 ('to be straight, upright, correct').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바로

바쁘다.etymology: Native Korean 으-irregular adjective meaning 'busy, pressed for time', descending from Middle Korean 밧브다 ('urgent, hard-pressed, busy') via glottalization (ㅅㅂ > ㅃ).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바쁘다

바삭하다.etymology: Native Korean ideophonic adjective and verb meaning 'crispy, crunchy; to rustle dryly', formed from the light-vowel mimetic root 바삭 ('sound or texture of dry leaves or crisp pastry breaking') plus -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바삭하다

morphemes.meaning: to be / make the sound of

바장조.etymology: Korean musical compound meaning 'F major', combining the native Korean hangul pitch letter 바 (assigned to the note F, the sixth letter in the 가-나-다-라-마-바-사 sequence corresponding to A-B-C-D-E-F-G) with Sino-Korean 장조 (長調, 'major key').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바장조

바짝.etymology: Native Korean mimetic adverb meaning 'closely, tightly, right up to; completely (dried up); tensely', an intensified light-vowel ideophone paired with 바싹.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바짝

바퀴.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'wheel; a turn or lap around a circuit', descending from Middle Korean 바회 / 바희 ('wheel') via Early Modern Korean consonantal strengthening (ㅎ + w > ㅋw).

history.meaning: wheel; counter for revolutions or laps

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 바퀴

박하차.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 박하차 (薄荷茶), meaning 'peppermint tea, mint tea', composed of 박하 (薄荷, 'peppermint, mentha') + 차 (茶, 'tea').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 박하차

밖.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'the outside, exterior; (with negative predicates) nothing but, only', descending from Middle Korean 밧 (with underlying stem 밧ㄱ-, attested in locative 밧긔 'outside').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밖

반.etymology: Sino-Korean noun representing two common homophones: (1) 반 (半, Middle Chinese *pwanH*), meaning 'half, middle, semi-'; and (2) 반 (班, Middle Chinese *pwan*), meaning 'class, group, team, shift'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반

반갑다.etymology: Native Korean ㅂ-irregular adjective meaning 'glad, delighted, welcome (upon meeting someone or hearing news)', derived from the Middle Korean verb 반기다 ('to rejoice at meeting, welcome warmly') + adjective-forming suffix -압다/-갑다.

history.meaning: to rejoice, welcome gladly -> glad, welcome

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반갑다

반값.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'half price', combining Sino-Korean 반 (半, 'half') with native Korean 값 ('price, value', Middle Korean 값).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반값

반듯하다.etymology: Native Korean adjective meaning 'straight, even, neat, upright, well-proportioned', formed from the light-vowel expressive root 반듯- ('straight and level without tilting') plus -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반듯하다

반죽.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'dough, batter, kneaded mixture (of flour, clay, or mortar)', attested in Early Modern Korean as 반쥭 / 반죽.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반죽

반짝반짝하다.etymology: Native Korean reduplicated ideophonic verb and adjective meaning 'to twinkle, sparkle, glitter continuously', formed from reduplicated mimetic 반짝반짝 ('repeated bright flashes or glints') + -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반짝반짝하다

반짝이다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to sparkle, twinkle, glitter, shine', derived from the mimetic root 반짝 ('sudden glint or flash of light') plus the verbalizing suffix -이다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반짝이다

반쯤.etymology: Hybrid compound meaning 'about half, halfway', formed from Sino-Korean 반 (半, 'half') plus the native Korean approximative suffix -쯤 ('about, approximately').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 반쯤

받다.etymology: Core native Korean regular verb meaning 'to receive, get, accept, take; to prop/catch from underneath', attested unchanged in form since Middle Korean 받다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 받다

받치다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to prop up, support from below, place a pad/tray underneath, hold up (an umbrella)', derived from 받- ('to receive, hold underneath') plus the intensive/causative suffix -치- (Middle Korean 받티다).

history.meaning: to support from underneath, hold up
to prop up, support, place a coaster/pad under

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 받치다

morphemes.meaning: to hold or receive from below

받침.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'support, prop, coaster, saucer, pad; (in Hangul orthography) a syllable-final consonant written underneath the vowel', derived from 받치다 ('to support from underneath') + nominalizer -ㅁ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 받침

morphemes.meaning: to prop up, support from below

발.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'foot, paw, step, leg (of furniture)', descending unchanged from Middle Korean 발. Also homophonous with native Korean 발 ('hanging blind or screen woven of bamboo splints or reeds', Middle Korean 발).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 발

발가락.etymology: Native Korean compound of 발 ('foot') and 가락 ('slender stick, spindle, digit').
발가락.notes: Built on the exact same pattern as 손가락 ('finger', 손 'hand' + 가락) and 젓가락 ('chopsticks').

발걸음.etymology: Native Korean compound of 발 ('foot') and 걸음 ('step, gait', nominalized with -음 from 걷다 'to walk').
발걸음.notes: Describes both audible footsteps and the tempo of someone's walk.

발뒤꿈치.etymology: Native Korean compound of 발 ('foot') + 뒤 ('back, rear') + 꿈치 ('protruding joint bend', cf. 팔꿈치 'elbow').
발뒤꿈치.notes: Clearly distinguishes the heel of the foot from the heel of a shoe (굽).

발목.etymology: Native Korean anatomical compound of 발 ('foot') and 목 ('neck, narrow constriction').

발소리.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'sound of footsteps, footfall, tread', formed from 발 ('foot') + 소리 ('sound', pronounced [발쏘리] with tensification).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 발소리

발전하다.etymology: Sino-Korean verb formed from 발전 (發展, 'development, progress, expansion', or 發電, 'electric power generation') plus -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 발전하다

발판.etymology: Hybrid compound combining native 발 ('foot') with Sino-Korean 판 (板, 'wooden board, plank').
발판.notes: Refers both to a low kitchen step stool and figuratively to a stepping-stone.

밝다.etymology: Native Korean adjective and verb descending from Middle Korean ᄇᆞᇰ다 ('bright, luminous, clear; to dawn; to be well-versed in'), with regular shift of ᆞ to ㅏ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밝다

밤.etymology: Native Korean noun representing two ancient homographs that were distinguished by pitch accent in Middle Korean: (1) 'night, nighttime' (Middle Korean 밤, low tone); and (2) 'chestnut' (Middle Korean 밤, long/rising tone, preserved as vowel length in standard pronunciation [밤:]).

history.form: 밤 (night, low tone) / 밤 (chestnut, rising tone)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밤

밤새.etymology: Native Korean compound noun and adverb meaning 'all night, throughout the night, overnight', contracted from 밤사이 (밤 'night' + 사이 'interval, duration, time between').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밤새

방.etymology: Sino-Korean noun 방 (房, Middle Chinese *bjang*), meaning 'room, chamber', borrowed early and used as the standard Korean word for an indoor room.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 방

방금.etymology: Sino-Korean noun and adverb 방금 (方今), meaning 'just now, a moment ago', formed from 方 (방, 'just now, at this point') + 今 (금, 'now, the present').

history.meaning: at this very moment, just now

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 방금

방석.etymology: Sino-Korean 방석 (方席), from 방 (方, 'square') + 석 (席, 'woven mat, seat').
방석.notes: Originally a square sedge or silk floor mat, now used for any square chair or floor cushion.

방울.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'drop (of water, rain, or sweat); small spherical bell; small round bulb/bead', descending from Middle Korean 방올 ('small bell; round drop') via vowel raising (오 > 우).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 방울

방해하다.etymology: Sino-Korean verb formed from 방해 (妨害, 'hindrance, obstruction, disturbance, interference') plus verbalizer -하다.

history.meaning: to disturb, interrupt, hinder, get in the way

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 방해하다

배.etymology: Polysemous Korean noun uniting three native Korean words from Middle Korean ᄇᆡ—(1) 'belly, stomach, abdomen', (2) 'boat, ship, vessel', and (3) 'pear'—alongside the Sino-Korean noun/bound noun 배 (倍, 'times, -fold, double').

history.meaning: stomach, belly; boat, ship; pear; -fold, double

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 배

배고프다.etymology: Native Korean compound adjective meaning 'hungry', formed from the subject noun 배 ('belly, stomach', Middle Korean ᄇᆡ) + adjective 고프다 ('to be hungry, famished, empty', Middle Korean 고프다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 배고프다

배관.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 배관 (配管), meaning 'plumbing, piping, pipework', formed from 配 (배, 'distribute, lay out') + 管 (관, 'pipe, tube').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 배관

배달.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 배달 (配達), meaning 'delivery, distribution (of mail, food, or goods)', composed of 配 (배, 'distribute, allocate') + 達 (달, 'reach, deliver').

history.meaning: distributing and delivering to a destination

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 배달

배우다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb meaning 'to learn, study, acquire knowledge or a skill', descending from Middle Korean ᄇᆡ호다 ('to learn').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 배우다

배치도.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 배치도 (配置圖), meaning 'layout plan, floor plan, arrangement diagram', formed from 배치 (配置, 'arrangement, placement') + 도 (圖, 'drawing, diagram, chart').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 배치도

백.etymology: Sino-Korean numeral 백 (百, Middle Chinese *paek*), meaning 'one hundred (100)'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 백

백설탕.etymology: Sino-Korean 백설탕 (白雪糖), prefixing 백- (白, 'white') to 설탕 (雪糖, 'snow-sugar').
백설탕.notes: Contrasts with 흑설탕 ('dark brown sugar') and 황설탕 ('golden raw sugar').

밸브.etymology: Borrowed from English valve ('device for regulating or stopping the flow of liquid or gas through a pipe'), ultimately from Latin valva ('leaf of a folding door').

history.meaning: flow-control device in piping or machinery

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 밸브

버너.etymology: Borrowed from English burner ('part of a stove, lamp, or portable camp stove that produces a flame').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 버너

버리다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to throw away, discard, abandon' (and as the auxiliary verb -어 버리다, marking complete or regrettable aspect), descending from Middle Korean ᄇᆞ리다 ('to discard, forsake').

history.meaning: to throw away, discard; (auxiliary) finish completely

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 버리다

버터.etymology: Borrowed from English butter, following standard Korean loanword orthography based on non-rhotic vowel endings (-er -> -어).
버터.notes: Combines with Sino-Korean prefixes such as 무염 버터 ('unsalted butter').

버튼.etymology: Borrowed from English button ('push-button switch on an appliance or interface; garment fastener').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 버튼

번.etymology: Sino-Korean bound noun and classifier 번 (番, Middle Chinese *phjwon*), meaning 'time, occurrence, turn; number in a series'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 번

번개.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'lightning, flash of lightning', descending from Middle Korean 번게 ('lightning', related to the flashing ideophonic root 번- as in 번쩍).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 번개

번거롭다.etymology: Hybrid adjective meaning 'troublesome, complicated, cumbersome, tedious', formed from Sino-Korean 번거 (煩劇 / 煩據, centered on 煩 'vexing, complicated, irksome') plus the native Korean adjective-forming suffix -롭다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 번거롭다

번지.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 번지 (番地), meaning 'lot number, street/house number in an address system', formed from 番 (번, 'number, order') + 地 (지, 'land, plot, site').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 번지

번째.etymology: Hybrid bound noun forming ordinal numbers ('-th time, -th in order'), combining Sino-Korean 번 (番, 'time, turn, order') with the native Korean ordinal suffix -째.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 번째

번호.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 번호 (番號), meaning 'number (telephone number, room number, serial number, code)', formed from 番 (번, 'turn, sequence') + 號 (호, 'number, mark, designation').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 번호

벌써.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'already, so soon', descending from Middle Korean 벌셔 ('already').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 벌써

법률.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 법률 (法律), meaning 'law, statute, legislation', composed of 法 (법, 'law, rule, principle') + 律 (률, 'statute, regulation, code', pronounced [범뉼] by nasalization).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 법률

벗기다.etymology: Native Korean causative verb meaning 'to peel, strip off, unwrap, take off (another's clothes or a cover)', derived from 벗다 ('to take off, shed') plus the causative suffix -기- (Middle Korean 벗기다).

history.meaning: to peel, strip, take off, uncover

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 벗기다

벗다.etymology: Native Korean regular verb meaning 'to take off, remove (clothing, shoes, headgear, glasses); to shed or rid oneself of', descending directly from Middle Korean 벗다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 벗다

베개.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'pillow, headrest', derived from the verb stem 베- (베다, 'to rest one's head on', Middle Korean 볘다) plus the native instrument-forming suffix -개 ('implement for doing', Middle Korean 볘개).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 베개

벨.etymology: Borrowed from English bell ('doorbell, buzzer, electric chime, or ringtone').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 벨

벽.etymology: Sino-Korean noun 벽 (壁, Middle Chinese *pek*), meaning 'wall, partition, barrier', deeply integrated into Korean since the Middle Korean period.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 벽

벽돌.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'brick', combining Sino-Korean 벽 (甓, 'brick, tile') with native Korean 돌 ('stone', Middle Korean 돌ㅎ) to reinforce the sense of a stone-like building block.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 벽돌

변호사.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 변호사 (辯護士), meaning 'lawyer, attorney-at-law', formed from 변호 (辯護, 'pleading and defending in law') + professional suffix -사 (士, 'licensed specialist, scholar').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 변호사

별.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'star, heavenly body', descending unchanged in form from Middle Korean 별 (with long/rising pitch [별:]). Also homophonous with the Sino-Korean determiner and prefix 별 (別, 'separate, special, extraordinary').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 별

별로.etymology: Hybrid adverb meaning '(with negative predicates) not particularly, not very much', formed from Sino-Korean 별 (別, 'special, particular, separate') plus the native Korean instrumental particle -로 ('by way of, as').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 별로

morphemes.meaning: by way of, in terms of

별점.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'star rating (for a restaurant, product, or film)', combining native Korean 별 ('star') with Sino-Korean 점 (點, 'point, score, mark'). Also homophonous with Sino-Korean 별점 (星占, 'astrology, star divination').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 별점

병.etymology: Sino-Korean noun representing two everyday homophones: (1) 병 (甁, Middle Chinese *beng*), meaning 'bottle, jar, vase'; and (2) 병 (病, Middle Chinese *bjaengH*, pronounced with a long vowel [병:]), meaning 'illness, disease, sickness'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 병

보관하다.etymology: Sino-Korean verb formed from 보관 (保管, 'keeping, storage, safekeeping') plus verbalizer -하다.

history.meaning: to protect and manage in storage
to keep, store, hold in custody

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보관하다

보금자리.etymology: Native Korean compound historically referring to a bird's warm nest, formed with 자리 ('place, spot').
보금자리.notes: Used figuratively in modern Korean for a cosy home or welcoming workplace where one settles in.

보내다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb meaning 'to send, dispatch; to spend or pass (time); to let go', attested unchanged in form since Middle Korean 보내다.

history.meaning: to send, dispatch, cause to go
to send; to spend (time); to see off

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보내다

보다.etymology: Core native Korean verb meaning 'to see, look at, watch, read; (as auxiliary -어 보다) to try doing', descending directly from Middle Korean 보다. Also used as a comparative particle and adverb meaning 'than; more' (grammaticalized from the verb 'to see/compare against').

history.meaning: to see, watch, look; (auxiliary) to try; than/more

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보다

보도.etymology: Sino-Korean compound representing two common homophones: (1) 보도 (步道), meaning 'sidewalk, pedestrian walkway, pavement', from 步 (보, 'walk, step') + 道 (도, 'road, way'); and (2) 보도 (報道), meaning 'news report, press coverage', from 報 (보, 'report, inform') + 道 (도, 'state, convey').

history.meaning: sidewalk, pavement (步道); news report (報道)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보도

보람.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'sense of worth, rewarding fruit of one's effort; identifying mark or tag', descending from Middle Korean 보람 ('visible mark or sign attached to an item for later recognition', derived from 보다 'to see').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보람

보리수.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 보리수 (菩提樹), meaning 'bodhi tree, linden tree', combining 보리 (菩提, the traditional Sino-Korean Buddhist transcription of Sanskrit bodhi 'awakening, enlightenment', where 提 is read 리) + 수 (樹, 'tree').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보리수

보면대.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 보면대 (譜面臺), meaning 'music stand, sheet-music rack', formed from 보면 (譜面, 'surface/page of a musical score') + 대 (臺, 'stand, platform, rack').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보면대

보이다.etymology: Native Korean passive and causative verb meaning 'to be seen, be visible, look/appear; to show, display', derived from 보다 ('to see') plus the suffix -이- (Middle Korean 보이다).

history.meaning: to be seen, appear; to show
to be visible, look; to show

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보이다

morphemes.meaning: to be seen / cause to see

보일러.notes: In South Korea, 보일러 specifically evokes the household hot-water and underfloor heating (온돌) boiler found in every home and guesthouse.

보일러실.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'boiler room, heating plant room', combining the English loanword 보일러 (boiler) with Sino-Korean 실 (室, 'room').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보일러실

보존법.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 보존법 (保存法), meaning 'preservation law/act; method of preservation', formed from 보존 (保存, 'preservation, conservation') + 법 (法, 'law, statute, method').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보존법

보통.etymology: Sino-Korean noun and adverb 보통 (普通), meaning 'usually, normally; ordinary, average', composed of 普 (보, 'universal, widespread') + 通 (통, 'common, pass through').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보통

보호받다.etymology: Hybrid compound passive verb meaning 'to be protected, receive protection', formed from Sino-Korean 보호 (保護, 'protection, care') + native Korean 받다 ('to receive').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 보호받다

복도.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 복도 (複道), meaning 'corridor, hallway, indoor passage', from 複 (복, 'double, covered') + 道 (도, 'way, passage, path').

history.meaning: covered passageway between rooms or buildings

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 복도

본명.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 본명 (本名), meaning 'real name, birth/legal name (as distinct from a stage name, pen name, or nickname)', formed from 本 (본, 'original, true') + 名 (명, 'name').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 본명

볼펜.etymology: Loanword from English ball(point) pen (clipped via ballpen, 'pen that dispenses ink over a small rotating metal ball at its point').

history.meaning: pen with a tiny rotating ball tip

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 볼펜

봄.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'spring (the first season of the year)', attested unchanged since Middle Korean 봄 (often connected etymologically by Korean historical linguists either to 보다 'to see/renew' or to 븕-/불- 'warmth, fire, sprouting').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 봄

봉지.etymology: Sino-Korean-derived noun 봉지 (封紙), meaning 'paper or plastic bag, pouch, packet', originally denoting a folded paper wrapper from 封 (봉, 'wrap, seal') + 紙 (지, 'paper').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 봉지

봉투.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 봉투 (封套), meaning 'envelope, paper bag', composed of 封 (봉, 'seal, close') + 套 (투, 'outer sleeve, case, wrapper').

history.meaning: outer paper sleeve that can be sealed

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 봉투

뵈다.etymology: Native Korean humble verb meaning 'to see, meet, greet (an elder or respected person)', descending from Middle Korean 뵈다 (derived from 보다 'to see' + -이-, and paired in Modern Korean with 뵙다).

history.meaning: to be seen by / humbly meet a superior

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뵈다

부담.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 부담 (負擔), from 부 (負, 'carry on the back') and 담 (擔, 'shoulder a load').
부담.notes: Both characters depict bearing physical weight, extended to emotional or financial pressure.

부동산.etymology: Sino-Korean legal and economic compound 부동산 (不動産), meaning 'real estate, immovable property (land and buildings)', formed from 不 (부, 'not') + 動 (동, 'move') + 産 (산, 'property, asset').

history.meaning: real estate, property; real estate agency

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부동산

부드럽다.etymology: Native Korean ㅂ-irregular adjective meaning 'soft, smooth, gentle, tender, mild', descending from Middle Korean 부들업다 / 부드럽다 (from the soft-texture root 부들- + adjective suffix -업다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부드럽다

부딪히다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to bump into, collide with, be struck against, encounter', derived from 부딪다 ('to strike against, hit') plus the passive/intensive suffix -히-.

history.meaning: to collide with, be bumped against
to bump into, crash into, face (a problem)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부딪히다

부러지다.etymology: Native Korean intransitive verb meaning 'to break, snap in two (of a stick, branch, bone, or rigid rod)', descending from Middle Korean 브러디다 (from 브르-/블- 'to snap, break' + inchoative -어디다 > -어지다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부러지다

부르다.etymology: Native Korean 르-irregular verb representing two Middle Korean verbs that merged through labial rounding (ㅡ > ㅜ): (1) 브르다 ('to call out, summon, sing a song, name'); and (2) 부르다 ('to be full, swollen, pregnant', as in 배가 부르다 'one's stomach is full').

history.meaning: to call, sing; to be full/swollen
to call, sing, name; to be full (of the stomach)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부르다

부리다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb descending from Middle Korean 부리다 with two main senses: (1) 'to work/employ (a person or animal); to wield, display, or indulge in (a skill, temper, or charm)'; and (2) 'to unload (cargo from a vehicle or vessel)'.

history.meaning: to employ, command, exercise; to unload
to wield, show off, act out; to manage; to unload

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부리다

부부.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 부부 (夫婦), meaning 'married couple, husband and wife', composed of 夫 (부, 'husband') + 婦 (부, 'wife').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부부

부어오르다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to swell up, puff up', combining the infinitive stem 부어- of the ㅅ-irregular verb 붓다 ('to swell', Middle Korean 븟다) with 오르다 ('to rise, go up').

history.meaning: to swell up, become inflamed or puffy

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부어오르다

부엌.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'kitchen', descending from Middle Korean 브섭 ('kitchen, hearth room') through lenition of intervocalic ㅸ (브섭 > 브업) and subsequent labial vowel rounding and final aspiration (부엌).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부엌

부엌문.etymology: Hybrid Korean compound joining native 부엌 ('kitchen') with Sino-Korean 문 (門, 'door').
부엌문.notes: Pronounced [부엉문]: final ㅋ neutralizes to [ㄱ] and assimilates to velar nasal [ㅇ] before ㅁ.

부족하다.etymology: Sino-Korean adjective formed from 부족 (不足, 'insufficiency, shortage, lack') plus the adjective-forming suffix -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부족하다

부탁하다.etymology: Sino-Korean verb formed from 부탁 (付託, 'request, favor, entrusting a matter to someone') plus verbalizer -하다.

history.meaning: to hand over and entrust a request
to ask a favor, request, entrust

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부탁하다

부풀다.etymology: Native Korean ㄹ-stem intransitive verb meaning 'to swell, rise (of bread dough), puff up, expand (of hopes or expectations)', formed from an intensive reduplicated/prefixed stem 부풀- related to 붓다 ('to swell') and 불다 ('to swell when soaked').

history.meaning: to swell, rise (of dough), puff up

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 부풀다

북카페.etymology: Compound loanword from English book and French/English café ('café equipped with bookshelves where visitors can read while drinking coffee').

history.meaning: café combined with a reading room or bookstore

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 북카페

분.etymology: Polysemous Korean bound noun and classifier: (1) native Korean honorific counter and bound noun meaning 'esteemed person' (attested since Middle Korean 분); and (2) Sino-Korean 분 (分, Middle Chinese *pjun*), meaning 'minute (of time or angle); part, share, portion'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 분

분명하다.etymology: Sino-Korean adjective formed from 분명 (分明, 'clear, distinct, plain, evident') plus the adjective-forming suffix -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 분명하다

분명히.etymology: Hybrid adverb meaning 'clearly, distinctly, definitely, surely', derived from Sino-Korean 분명 (分明, 'clear, evident') plus the native Korean adverbial suffix -히.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 분명히

분수대.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 분수대 (噴水臺), meaning 'water fountain, fountain basin', formed from 분수 (噴水, 'spouting water, fountain') + 대 (臺, 'platform, basin, stand').

history.meaning: structure or basin for a water fountain

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 분수대

분실물.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 분실물 (紛失物), meaning 'lost article, lost-and-found item', formed from 분실 (紛失, 'losing or misplacing an item') + 물 (物, 'thing, object').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 분실물

분짜리.etymology: Hybrid compound bound noun meaning 'something of (so many) minutes in duration', combining Sino-Korean 분 (分, 'minute') with the native Korean suffix -짜리 ('having the value, measure, or duration of').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 분짜리

morphemes.meaning: having the measure or value of

분필.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 분필 (粉筆), from 분 (粉, 'powder') and 필 (筆, 'writing brush, pen').
분필.notes: Shares 필 (筆, 'writing implement') with 연필 (鉛筆, 'pencil').

불.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'fire, flame, light/lamp', descending from Middle Korean 블 ('fire') through Early Modern Korean labial rounding of ㅡ to ㅜ after the bilabial stop ㅂ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 불

불꽃.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'flame, blaze, spark, fireworks', literally 'flower of fire', combining 불 ('fire', Middle Korean 블) + 꽃 ('flower, blossom', Middle Korean 곶).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 불꽃

불빛.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'firelight, lamplight, glow of a light', formed from 불 ('fire, lamp', Middle Korean 블) + 빛 ('light, ray', Middle Korean 빛).

history.meaning: light of a fire or lamp

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 불빛

불쌍하다.etymology: Adjective meaning 'pitiful, poor, pathetic, arousing sympathy', attested in Early Modern Korean as 불샹ᄒᆞ다 (widely traced to Sino-Korean 不祥 'unfortunate, inauspicious' + -하다, which underwent semantic shift to 'pitiful' and glottalization to 불쌍하다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 불쌍하다

불안하다.etymology: Sino-Korean adjective formed from 불안 (不安, 'uneasiness, anxiety, instability') plus the adjective-forming suffix -하다.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 불안하다

불어내다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to blow away, blow out/off (dust, shavings, or water)', combining 불다 ('to blow with the breath or wind', Middle Korean 블다) + 내다 ('to put forth, remove').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 불어내다

불투명.etymology: Sino-Korean negator 불- (不, 'not') prefixed to 투명 (透明, 'transparent': 투 透 'pass through' + 명 明 'bright, clear').
불투명.notes: Describes frosted conservatory or lamp glass that diffuses light without allowing a direct view through.

붓.etymology: Early nativized Korean noun meaning 'writing brush, ink brush, paintbrush', attested in Middle Korean as 븟, an ancient borrowing from Old/Middle Chinese 筆 (*pit*, 'writing brush') that entered Korean prior to the regular Sino-Korean reading 필 (筆).

history.meaning: writing or painting brush (early loan from 筆)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 붓

붓다.etymology: Native Korean ㅅ-irregular verb uniting two Middle Korean verbs that merged after labial vowel rounding (ㅡ > ㅜ): (1) 븥다 / 븟다 ('to pour liquid, cast metal'); and (2) 븟다 ('to swell, become puffy or inflamed').

history.meaning: to pour liquid; to swell up
to pour; to swell, puff up

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 붓다

붙다.etymology: Native Korean regular verb meaning 'to stick to, adhere, be attached; to pass (an examination); to catch (fire)', descending from Middle Korean 붙다 / 븉다 ('to adhere, join, stick').

history.meaning: to stick, adhere; to pass (a test); to ignite

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 붙다

블록.etymology: Borrowed from English block ('solid piece of wood, stone, or concrete; building block; city block').

history.meaning: solid rectangular building unit or city section
block (building block, paving block, city block)

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 블록

비.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'rain', attested unchanged in form since Middle Korean 비. Also homophonous with native Korean 비 ('broom') and Sino-Korean nouns 비 (費 'cost, fee'; 比 'ratio, comparison'; 碑 'stone monument').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비

비교하다.etymology: Sino-Korean 비교 (比較, 비 'compare side by side' + 교 'measure against') + -하다.

비누.etymology: Native Korean noun meaning 'soap', descending from Middle Korean 비누 ('washing powder made from ground soybeans and herbs, later bar soap').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비누

비눗물.etymology: Korean compound of 비누 ('soap', an early loanword via Portuguese sabão) + compound linker 사이시옷 (-ㅅ-) + native 물 ('water').
비눗물.notes: Pronounced [비눈물] as 사이시옷 triggers nasal insertion before ㅁ.

비다.etymology: Native Korean intransitive verb meaning 'to be empty, vacant, hollow, unoccupied', descending from Middle Korean 븨다 ('to be empty, void') via monophthongization (ㅢ > ㅣ after ㅂ).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비다

비밀.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 비밀 (秘密), meaning 'secret, mystery, confidentiality', composed of 秘 (비, 'secret, hidden') + 密 (밀, 'covert, close, confidential').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비밀

비상.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 비상 (非常), meaning 'emergency, contingency; extraordinary', literally 'not ordinary', from 非 (비, 'not') + 常 (상, 'ordinary, constant'). Also homophonous with 비상 (飛翔, 'soaring, flight').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비상

비상용.etymology: Sino-Korean 비상 (非常, literally 'not ordinary' -> 'emergency') plus suffix -용 (用, 'for the use of').
비상용.notes: Productive -용 (用) suffix also forms 가정용 ('household use') and 상업용 ('commercial use').

비스킷.etymology: Borrowed from English biscuit ('crisp, flat baked cookie or cracker'), ultimately from Old French bescuit ('twice-cooked bread').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비스킷

비슷하다.etymology: Native Korean adjective meaning 'similar, alike, resembling, close to', attested in Early Modern Korean as 비슷ᄒᆞ다 (from the root 비슷- + -하다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비슷하다

비싸다.etymology: Native Korean adjective meaning 'expensive, costly', descending from Middle Korean 값싸다 / 빗싸다, originally a compound of 빚/값 ('price, value') + 싸다 (which in Middle Korean meant 'to be worth, have a high price'; when simplex 싸다 later shifted to 'cheap', the compound 비싸다 preserved the older sense 'high-priced, expensive').

history.meaning: high-priced, costly (from 빚 'price' + 싸다 'to be worth/costly')

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비싸다

비우다.etymology: Native Korean causative verb meaning 'to empty, clear out, drain, vacate', derived from 비다 ('to be empty', Middle Korean 븨다) plus the causative suffix -우- (Middle Korean 븨오다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비우다

비율.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 비율 (比率), meaning 'ratio, proportion, percentage, rate', formed from 比 (비, 'compare') + 率 (율/률, 'rate, proportion', written 율 after a vowel).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비율

비추다.etymology: Native Korean transitive/causative verb meaning 'to shine (a light) upon, illuminate, reflect in a mirror', descending from Middle Korean 비취다 / 비초다 (causative derivative built on 빛 'light').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비추다

비치다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to shine, be reflected, show through translucently', descending from Middle Korean 비취다 ('to shine, gleam, be reflected', derived from 빛 'light').

history.meaning: to shine, be reflected, show through
to shine, be reflected, be seen through

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비치다

비키다.etymology: Native Korean verb meaning 'to step aside, move out of the way, yield passage', attested in Early Modern Korean as 비키다 (derived from the root 빗- 'oblique, sideways' + causative/verbal suffix -키-).

history.meaning: to step aside, clear the way
to step aside, move out of the way

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비키다

비품실.etymology: Sino-Korean compound 비품실 (備品室), meaning 'supply room, equipment storage room', formed from 비품 (備品, 'furnishings, fixtures, supplies') + 실 (室, 'room').

history.meaning: room for storing fixtures and supplies

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 비품실

빌다.etymology: Native Korean ㄹ-stem verb descending from Middle Korean 빌다 with two principal senses: (1) 'to pray, wish for, beg, apologize'; and (2) 'to borrow, rent' (the base verb from which 빌리다 is derived).

history.meaning: to pray, beg, wish; to borrow
to pray, wish, beg for forgiveness; to borrow

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빌다

빌려주다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to lend, loan', formed from 빌리다 ('to borrow/lend', stem 빌려-) plus the benefactive auxiliary verb 주다 ('to give').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빌려주다

빗물.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'rainwater', formed from 비 ('rain') + genitive interfix -ㅅ- (사이시옷) + 물 ('water', Middle Korean 빗믈).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빗물

빗방울.etymology: Transparent native Korean compound of 비 ('rain') + 사이시옷 (-ㅅ-) + 방울 ('drop, bead').
빗방울.notes: Shares 비 + 사이시옷 with 빗물 ('rainwater') and 빗소리 ('sound of rain').

빗소리.etymology: Native Korean compound from 비 ('rain') + 사이시옷 (-ㅅ-) + 소리 ('sound').
빗소리.notes: The linking ㅅ tenses the following consonant in speech: [빋쏘리].

빗속.etymology: Native Korean compound noun meaning 'in the rain, the midst of falling rain', formed from 비 ('rain') + genitive interfix -ㅅ- (사이시옷) + 속 ('inside, midst').

history.meaning: in the rain, midst of the rain

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빗속

빛.etymology: Core native Korean noun meaning 'light, ray, beam; color, hue, lustre', attested unchanged in form since Middle Korean 빛.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빛

빛나다.etymology: Native Korean compound verb meaning 'to shine, gleam, sparkle, be radiant', formed from 빛 ('light, lustre') + 나다 ('to come forth, arise', Middle Korean 빛나다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빛나다

빠르다.etymology: Native Korean 르-irregular adjective meaning 'fast, quick, swift, early', descending from Middle Korean ᄈᆞᄅᆞ다 ('fast, rapid').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빠르다

빠지다.etymology: Native Korean intransitive verb meaning 'to fall into (water, a pit, or a state); to fall out, be omitted/missing; to be absorbed in; to drain out', descending from Middle Korean ᄢᅡ디다 ('to fall into, sink, drop out').

history.meaning: to fall into; to fall out, be left out; to be absorbed in

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빠지다

빤히.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'staringly, fixedly; obviously, clearly', derived from the light-vowel adjective 빤하다 ('bright, obvious, staring', glottalized counterpart of 반하다/번하다) + adverbial suffix -히.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빤히

빨간색.etymology: Hybrid compound noun meaning 'red color, bright red', combining the adnominal form 빨간 of the native Korean color adjective 빨갛다 ('bright red') with Sino-Korean 색 (色, 'color').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빨간색

빨갛다.etymology: Native Korean ㅎ-irregular color adjective meaning 'bright red, vivid crimson', formed as the light-vowel, glottalized intensive counterpart of 발갛다 and 붉다 ('red', Middle Korean 븕다).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빨갛다

빨리.etymology: Native Korean adverb meaning 'quickly, fast, Hurry, soon', derived from the adjective stem 빠르- (빠르다, 'fast', Middle Korean ᄈᆞᄅᆞ다) plus the adverbial suffix -이 (Middle Korean ᄈᆞᆯ리).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빨리

빵.etymology: Borrowed via Japanese パン (pan) from 16th-century Portuguese pão ('bread'), ultimately from Latin pānis.
빵.notes: One of the earliest European-root loanwords in Korean, spelled with tense ㅃ to reflect the unaspirated Romance p.

빼다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb meaning 'to pull out, extract, remove, subtract, leave out', descending from Middle Korean ᄲᅢ다 (causative counterpart of ᄢᅡ디다 > 빠지다 'to fall out').

history.meaning: to pull out, draw out, extract
to pull out, remove, subtract, exclude

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 빼다

뻑뻑하다.etymology: Native Korean ideophonic adjective meaning 'stiff, tight, not sliding or turning smoothly (of a drawer, door, or hinge); dry and thick; dry (of eyes)', formed from the reduplicated dark-vowel mimetic root 뻑뻑 + -하다.

history.meaning: stiff, tight, hard to move; dry and thick

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뻑뻑하다

뻗다.etymology: Native Korean regular verb meaning 'to stretch out, extend, reach out, spread', descending from Middle Korean 벋다 ('to stretch, extend') with initial consonant tensification (ㅂ > ㅃ).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뻗다

뽀송하다.etymology: Native Korean expressive adjective meaning 'soft, dry, and fluffy (pleasantly free of dampness, as of freshly laundered towels or dry skin)', formed as the tensified light-vowel counterpart of 보송하다 + -하다.

history.meaning: dry and soft -> pleasantly dry, fluffy, and fresh

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뽀송하다

뽑다.etymology: Native Korean regular verb meaning 'to pull out, extract, uproot, draw out; to select, recruit, elect', descending from Middle Korean ᄲᅩᆸ다 ('to pull out, draw forth').

history.meaning: to pull out, extract; to pick, select, print/dispense

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뽑다

뿌듯하다.etymology: Native Korean expressive adjective meaning 'proud and deeply satisfied, fulfilled, full to capacity', formed from the tensified stem 뿌듯- (intensive counterpart of 부듯- 'tightly filled') plus -하다.

history.meaning: tightly full -> swelling with pride or satisfaction

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뿌듯하다

morphemes.meaning: full to the brim, swelling with satisfaction

뿌리다.etymology: Native Korean transitive verb meaning 'to sprinkle, scatter, strew, spray, shower', descending from Middle Korean ᄲᅳ리다 ('to sprinkle, scatter') via labial vowel rounding (ㅡ > ㅜ after ㅃ).

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뿌리다

뿐.etymology: Native Korean bound noun and postpositional particle meaning 'only, merely, nothing but', descending directly from Middle Korean ᄲᅮᆫ.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 뿐

사.etymology: Sino-Korean numeral 사 (四, Middle Chinese *sijH*), meaning 'four (4)'.

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 사

사과.etymology: Sino-Korean compound representing two common homophones: (1) 사과 (沙果), meaning 'apple' (literally 'sandy/crisp-textured fruit', from 沙 'sand/granular' + 果 'fruit'); and (2) 사과 (謝過), meaning 'apology' (from 謝 'apologize, express regret' + 過 'fault, transgression').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 사과

사과드리다.etymology: Hybrid humble compound verb meaning 'to apologize, offer an apology (to a respected person)', combining Sino-Korean 사과 (謝過, 'apology') with the native Korean humble benefactive verb 드리다 ('to give/offer to a superior').

sources.title: NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary — 사과드리다

morphemes.meaning: to offer, give to a superior
